scenarios.title: Credit Card Due Reminder Notification
scenarios.description: Verify that an automated due reminder notification is sent to the cardholder before the payment due date with the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system automatically sends a due reminder notification to the cardholder containing the upcoming payment due date and the last 4 digits of the credit card number for identification purposes.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists in the system.
2. Credit card is active and in good standing.
3. Payment due date is configured in the system.
4. Notification service is enabled and configured.
5. Cardholder has valid contact information (email/phone).
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Set up a credit card account with a specific due date (e.g., 15th of each month).
2. Configure the system to send reminder notifications X days before the due date (e.g., 5 days before).
3. Wait for the reminder trigger date to occur or simulate the date.
4. Verify that the notification is generated by the system.
5. Check the notification content for due date information.
6. Verify that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed.
7. Confirm the notification is sent to the cardholder's registered contact channels.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Notification is automatically triggered at the configured time before the due date.
2. Notification contains the payment due date clearly stated.
3. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed (e.g., **** 1234).
4. The full credit card number is NOT visible anywhere in the notification.
5. Notification is successfully delivered to the cardholder via configured channels (email/SMS).
6. The notification includes relevant payment instructions or payment amount due.

scenarios.title: Overdue Balance Alert Generation
scenarios.description: Verify that an overdue balance alert is sent to the cardholder when payment due date is missed, including the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system automatically sends an overdue balance alert notification to the cardholder after the payment due date has passed without payment, including consequences information and the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists with an active credit card.
2. Payment due date has passed without payment being received.
3. Account status is marked as overdue in the system.
4. Notification service is operational.
5. Cardholder contact information is available.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Create a credit card account with a due date.
2. Allow the due date to pass without processing any payment.
3. System should detect the missed payment (can be simulated by advancing system date).
4. Monitor for automatic generation of overdue alert.
5. Retrieve the overdue balance alert notification.
6. Verify the alert content includes overdue balance amount.
7. Check that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed.
8. Verify potential consequences are mentioned in the alert.
9. Confirm notification delivery to the cardholder.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Overdue balance alert is automatically triggered after the due date passes.
2. Alert clearly states the overdue balance amount.
3. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are visible (e.g., **** 5678).
4. Full credit card number is never displayed.
5. Alert includes information about potential consequences (late fees, interest charges, credit score impact).
6. Notification is successfully sent to the cardholder's registered contact information.
7. Alert timestamp indicates it was sent after the due date.

scenarios.title: Collection Notification for Significantly Delinquent Account
scenarios.description: Verify that formal collection notifications are sent when an account becomes significantly delinquent, including the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system escalates to formal collection notifications when an account reaches a significantly delinquent status, detailing the amount owed, additional charges, and the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists with overdue balance.
2. Account has reached the threshold for 'significantly delinquent' status (e.g., 60+ days overdue).
3. Previous reminder and overdue alerts have been sent.
4. Collection notification rules are configured in the system.
5. Notification service is active.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Set up a credit card account with overdue balance exceeding the delinquency threshold.
2. Configure the system to escalate to collection notification after X days of non-payment (e.g., 60 days).
3. Simulate or wait for the delinquency threshold to be reached.
4. Verify that the system generates a formal collection notification.
5. Review the notification content for total amount owed.
6. Check for additional charges (late fees, interest) in the notification.
7. Verify only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are included.
8. Confirm the formal/legal tone of the notification.
9. Verify delivery to the cardholder.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Collection notification is automatically generated when account reaches significantly delinquent status.
2. Notification has a formal tone appropriate for collection purposes.
3. Total amount owed is clearly detailed including principal balance.
4. Additional charges (late fees, accumulated interest) are itemized.
5. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed (e.g., **** 9012).
6. Full credit card number is not visible anywhere.
7. Notification includes deadline for payment and consequences of continued non-payment.
8. Notification is successfully delivered via registered channels.

scenarios.title: Payment Plan Proposal for Unable-to-Pay Cardholder
scenarios.description: Verify that a payment plan proposal is generated and sent to cardholders unable to pay the full overdue balance, including the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system can generate and send a payment plan proposal outlining a structured repayment schedule with reduced interest rates or fees for cardholders unable to pay the full overdue amount at once.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists with significant overdue balance.
2. Cardholder has contacted the bank or indicated inability to pay full amount.
3. Account is eligible for payment plan based on bank policies.
4. Payment plan terms are configured in the system.
5. Notification service is operational.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Create a scenario where a cardholder has an overdue balance and requests payment assistance.
2. Initiate payment plan proposal generation in the system.
3. Configure payment plan parameters (duration, installment amounts, interest rate reduction).
4. Generate the payment plan proposal document/notification.
5. Review proposal content for structured repayment schedule details.
6. Verify reduced interest rates or fees are mentioned.
7. Check that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed.
8. Verify terms and conditions are included.
9. Confirm delivery to the cardholder.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Payment plan proposal is successfully generated.
2. Proposal includes a clear, structured repayment schedule with specific dates and amounts.
3. Reduced interest rates or waived fees are clearly stated.
4. Total amount to be repaid and payment frequency are specified.
5. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are visible (e.g., **** 3456).
6. Full credit card number is never displayed.
7. Terms and conditions of the payment plan are included.
8. Acceptance instructions are provided to the cardholder.
9. Proposal is delivered successfully via appropriate channels.

scenarios.title: Collection Agency Involvement Notification
scenarios.description: Verify that collection agency is involved and provided with the last 4 digits of the credit card number when cardholder fails to respond to previous notifications.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system escalates to collection agency involvement when the cardholder fails to respond to previous notifications and reminders, and that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are shared with the agency.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists with significant overdue balance.
2. Multiple previous notifications have been sent without response.
3. Account has reached the threshold for collection agency referral (e.g., 90+ days overdue).
4. Collection agency partnership is configured in the system.
5. Data sharing protocols are established.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Set up a delinquent account that has not responded to previous notifications.
2. Configure the system to escalate to collection agency after X days of non-response.
3. Trigger or simulate the collection agency referral threshold.
4. Verify that the system initiates collection agency involvement.
5. Check the data package being sent to the collection agency.
6. Verify that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are included in the shared data.
7. Confirm that full credit card number is NOT shared.
8. Verify notification is sent to cardholder about collection agency involvement.
9. Check that the notification includes agency contact information.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Collection agency involvement is triggered automatically when criteria are met.
2. Data package sent to collection agency includes account details and overdue amount.
3. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are included in shared data (e.g., **** 7890).
4. Full credit card number and other sensitive payment data are NOT shared.
5. Cardholder receives notification about collection agency involvement.
6. Notification includes collection agency name and contact information.
7. Notification maintains professional but firm tone.
8. System logs the escalation event with timestamp.
9. Account status is updated to reflect collection agency involvement.

scenarios.title: Legal Action Initiation Documentation
scenarios.description: Verify that legal action documentation is properly generated in extreme cases of non-payment, including only the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system can initiate legal action process in extreme cases of default, ensuring all legal documentation includes only the last 4 digits of the credit card number for identification purposes.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account exists with severe delinquency.
2. All previous collection efforts have been exhausted.
3. Account meets criteria for legal action (e.g., 120+ days overdue, significant amount).
4. Legal department approval process is configured.
5. Legal documentation templates are available in the system.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Create a severely delinquent account that has exhausted all collection efforts.
2. Configure the system criteria for legal action initiation.
3. Trigger or simulate the legal action threshold being met.
4. Initiate legal action documentation process in the system.
5. Generate legal documentation (notices, demand letters, court filings preparation).
6. Review all legal documents for credit card number references.
7. Verify that only the last 4 digits of the credit card number appear in all documents.
8. Confirm full credit card number is never displayed in plain text.
9. Verify cardholder notification about legal action.
10. Check documentation completeness and legal compliance.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Legal action process is successfully initiated when criteria are met.
2. All legal documentation is generated according to templates.
3. Only the last 4 digits of the credit card number appear in all documents (e.g., **** 2468).
4. Full credit card number is never visible in any legal documentation.
5. Documents include complete account history, amounts owed, and collection attempts made.
6. Cardholder receives formal notification about impending legal action.
7. Notification includes deadline for payment to avoid legal proceedings.
8. All documentation complies with legal and regulatory requirements.
9. System maintains audit trail of legal action initiation.
10. Appropriate internal approvals are documented.

scenarios.title: Security Validation - Last 4 Digits Display Only
scenarios.description: Verify that across all collection lifecycle communications, only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are displayed and full number is never exposed.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system enforces security protocols to display only the last 4 digits of credit card numbers across all collection lifecycle communications and never exposes the full credit card number in plain text.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Multiple cardholder accounts with active credit cards exist.
2. Accounts are at various stages of the collection lifecycle.
3. All notification types are configured and active.
4. Security policies are implemented in the system.
5. Access to notification templates and output.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Generate all types of collection lifecycle notifications for test accounts.
2. Review each notification type (reminder, overdue alert, collection notice, payment plan, agency involvement, legal action).
3. Search each notification for credit card number references.
4. Verify format of credit card number display (should be masked except last 4 digits).
5. Check email notifications for credit card number display.
6. Check SMS notifications for credit card number display.
7. Check printed documents for credit card number display.
8. Review system logs and database records to ensure full numbers are encrypted.
9. Attempt to access full credit card number through various system interfaces.
10. Verify that only authorized, audited processes can access full number.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. All notifications display credit card numbers in masked format (e.g., **** **** **** 1234).
2. Only the last 4 digits are visible in any customer-facing communication.
3. Full credit card number never appears in plain text in any notification.
4. Email, SMS, and printed documents all follow the same masking rules.
5. System enforces masking at the data presentation layer.
6. Full credit card numbers are encrypted in database storage.
7. Access to full credit card numbers requires special authorization and is logged.
8. Masking cannot be bypassed through UI or API calls without proper authentication.
9. Security validation passes for all notification channels.
10. Compliance with PCI-DSS and data protection regulations is maintained.

scenarios.title: Collection Lifecycle Progression Sequence
scenarios.description: Verify that the collection lifecycle progresses through the correct sequence from reminder to legal action based on configured timelines and cardholder responses.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system correctly progresses through the collection lifecycle stages in the proper sequence, respecting configured timelines and adjusting based on cardholder payments or responses.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Test cardholder account exists with active credit card.
2. All collection lifecycle stages are configured with appropriate timelines.
3. Notification services are operational.
4. Payment processing capabilities are available.
5. System can be time-advanced for testing purposes.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Create a new credit card account with a defined due date.
2. Document the configured timelines for each stage (e.g., reminder at -5 days, overdue at +1 day, collection at +30 days, etc.).
3. Allow due date to approach and verify reminder notification is sent.
4. Allow due date to pass without payment.
5. Verify overdue alert is sent at the correct time.
6. Continue non-payment scenario and verify progression to collection notification.
7. Verify progression to collection agency involvement at configured threshold.
8. Verify progression to legal action at final threshold.
9. Test interruption scenarios: make partial payment and verify stage adjustment.
10. Verify that each stage includes last 4 digits of credit card number appropriately.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Reminder notification is sent at the configured time before due date.
2. Overdue alert is sent immediately after due date passes (or next business day).
3. Collection notification is sent after configured delinquency period (e.g., 30-60 days).
4. Collection agency involvement occurs at next threshold (e.g., 90 days).
5. Legal action initiation occurs at final threshold (e.g., 120 days).
6. Each stage transition is logged with timestamp and reason.
7. Making payment or contact pauses or resets the lifecycle appropriately.
8. All notifications at each stage include only last 4 digits of credit card number.
9. No stage is skipped in the progression.
10. System maintains complete audit trail of lifecycle progression.

scenarios.title: Payment Plan Acceptance and Execution
scenarios.description: Verify that when a cardholder accepts a payment plan proposal, the system properly executes the plan and adjusts the collection lifecycle accordingly.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system can process payment plan acceptance, set up scheduled payments, and appropriately pause or modify the collection lifecycle while the plan is in good standing.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder account with overdue balance exists.
2. Payment plan proposal has been generated and sent.
3. Payment processing capabilities are configured.
4. Scheduled payment functionality is available.
5. Collection lifecycle can be paused/modified by system.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Generate and send a payment plan proposal to a delinquent cardholder.
2. Simulate cardholder acceptance of the payment plan.
3. Verify system creates scheduled payment entries based on the plan.
4. Check that collection lifecycle notifications are paused or modified.
5. Verify first scheduled payment is processed on due date.
6. Confirm account status reflects active payment plan.
7. Test scenario where cardholder misses a payment plan installment.
8. Verify system reactivates collection lifecycle if payment plan defaults.
9. Verify all communications include last 4 digits of credit card number.
10. Test successful completion of payment plan.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Payment plan acceptance is successfully recorded in the system.
2. Scheduled payments are created according to the plan terms.
3. Collection lifecycle notifications are paused while plan is in good standing.
4. First and subsequent payments are automatically processed on schedule.
5. Account status is updated to 'Payment Plan Active' or similar.
6. If payment plan installment is missed, system sends warning notification.
7. After multiple missed installments, full collection lifecycle resumes.
8. Upon successful completion of payment plan, account status returns to good standing.
9. All payment plan communications display only last 4 digits of credit card (e.g., **** 5432).
10. Payment plan history is maintained in account records.

scenarios.title: Multi-Channel Notification Delivery
scenarios.description: Verify that collection lifecycle notifications are delivered successfully across multiple communication channels (email, SMS, mail) with consistent content and security.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that all collection lifecycle notifications can be delivered through multiple channels based on cardholder preferences and availability, maintaining consistent messaging and security across all channels.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Cardholder accounts exist with various contact preferences configured.
2. Email, SMS, and postal mail services are configured and operational.
3. Multiple channel notification templates are available.
4. Test accounts have valid contact information for each channel.
5. Notification tracking is enabled.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Configure test accounts with different channel preferences (email only, SMS only, both, plus mail).
2. Trigger a due reminder notification for each test account.
3. Verify notification is sent via the appropriate channel(s) for each account.
4. Check email notification content, format, and last 4 digits display.
5. Check SMS notification content, format, and last 4 digits display.
6. Check postal mail content, format, and last 4 digits display.
7. Verify consistency of messaging across all channels.
8. Verify delivery confirmation is received for each channel.
9. Test fallback scenarios (if email fails, try SMS).
10. Repeat for other lifecycle stages (overdue, collection, etc.).
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Notifications are successfully sent via all configured channels.
2. Email notifications are properly formatted with all required information.
3. SMS notifications are concise but contain essential information including last 4 digits.
4. Postal mail is generated and queued for mailing service.
5. All channels display only last 4 digits of credit card number (e.g., **** 6789).
6. Content is consistent across channels with appropriate formatting for each medium.
7. Delivery confirmations are received and logged.
8. Fallback mechanism activates if primary channel fails.
9. Cardholder preferences are respected.
10. All notification attempts are logged in the system with timestamps and status.

scenarios.title: Collection Notification Performance Under Load
scenarios.description: Verify that the collection lifecycle notification system can handle high volumes of notifications during peak processing times without degradation.
scenarios.testDescription: Test the system's ability to process and send large volumes of collection lifecycle notifications simultaneously while maintaining acceptable performance levels and delivery times.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. System is configured with production-level hardware/resources.
2. Large dataset of test accounts is available (thousands to millions).
3. Performance monitoring tools are in place.
4. Notification services are operational.
5. Load testing tools are configured.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Create a large dataset of accounts due for various collection lifecycle notifications (e.g., 100,000 accounts).
2. Configure monitoring for system resources (CPU, memory, network, database).
3. Set up performance metrics collection (notification generation time, delivery time, throughput).
4. Trigger batch notification processing for all accounts.
5. Monitor system resource utilization during processing.
6. Measure time taken to generate all notifications.
7. Measure time taken to deliver all notifications.
8. Check for any failed notifications or errors.
9. Verify notification queue processing efficiency.
10. Validate that all notifications still display only last 4 digits correctly under load.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. System successfully processes all notifications within acceptable time frame (e.g., within 2 hours for 100,000 notifications).
2. CPU utilization remains below 80% during peak processing.
3. Memory usage remains stable without memory leaks.
4. Database response times remain within acceptable thresholds (e.g., <500ms per query).
5. Notification throughput meets minimum requirements (e.g., 500+ notifications per minute).
6. Error rate remains below acceptable threshold (e.g., <0.1%).
7. All notifications maintain correct format and security (last 4 digits only).
8. System remains responsive to other operations during batch processing.
9. Notification queue does not experience significant backlog.
10. No data corruption or security breaches occur under load.

scenarios.title: Data Security and Encryption for Credit Card Information
scenarios.description: Verify that full credit card numbers are encrypted at rest and in transit, and that only the last 4 digits are ever decrypted for display purposes.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system implements proper encryption for credit card numbers in storage and transmission, ensuring PCI-DSS compliance and that decryption only occurs for authorized purposes, never for customer-facing notifications.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. System has encryption mechanisms implemented.
2. Database encryption is configured.
3. TLS/SSL is enabled for all communications.
4. Security scanning tools are available.
5. Access to database and network traffic monitoring.
6. Test accounts with credit card data exist.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Review database schema and verify credit card numbers are stored in encrypted format.
2. Query database directly and verify full numbers are not visible in plain text.
3. Use network monitoring tools to capture traffic during notification generation.
4. Verify that credit card data in transit is encrypted (TLS 1.2 or higher).
5. Attempt to access credit card data through application logs.
6. Verify that only last 4 digits are logged, not full numbers.
7. Check notification generation code to ensure masking occurs before display.
8. Verify encryption key management and rotation policies.
9. Test that decryption requires proper authentication and authorization.
10. Run security vulnerability scans focusing on data exposure.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Credit card numbers are stored using strong encryption (AES-256 or equivalent).
2. Direct database queries show encrypted data only, not plain text numbers.
3. All network traffic containing credit card data uses TLS 1.2 or higher encryption.
4. Application logs never contain full credit card numbers.
5. Only last 4 digits appear in any logs or notifications.
6. Decryption requires proper authentication, authorization, and is audited.
7. Encryption keys are properly managed and rotated according to policy.
8. No credit card data is exposed in temporary files or cache.
9. Security scans reveal no vulnerabilities related to credit card data exposure.
10. System achieves PCI-DSS compliance for data protection requirements.

scenarios.title: Audit Trail and Compliance Logging
scenarios.description: Verify that all collection lifecycle activities are properly logged with complete audit trails for compliance and regulatory purposes.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the system maintains comprehensive audit logs for all collection lifecycle activities, including notification generation, delivery, cardholder responses, and any system or user actions related to the collection process.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Audit logging functionality is enabled.
2. Log storage has sufficient capacity.
3. Test accounts at various collection lifecycle stages exist.
4. Log analysis tools are available.
5. Regulatory compliance requirements are documented.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Trigger various collection lifecycle events (reminder, overdue alert, collection notice, etc.).
2. Verify that each event generates an audit log entry.
3. Check log entries for completeness (timestamp, user/system actor, action, account identifier, outcome).
4. Verify that logs include only last 4 digits of credit card numbers.
5. Test that logs capture failed notification attempts and reasons.
6. Verify logging of cardholder responses and payments.
7. Check that system changes to collection lifecycle are logged.
8. Verify log retention meets regulatory requirements.
9. Test log querying and reporting capabilities.
10. Verify log integrity and tamper-proof mechanisms.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. All collection lifecycle events are logged with complete details.
2. Log entries include timestamp, user/system identifier, action taken, and outcome.
3. Logs contain only last 4 digits of credit card numbers, never full numbers.
4. Failed notifications are logged with specific error reasons.
5. Cardholder payments and responses are logged with transaction details.
6. System configuration changes affecting collection lifecycle are logged.
7. Logs are retained for required period (typically 7+ years for financial records).
8. Logs are stored in tamper-proof format with integrity verification.
9. Log queries can retrieve specific events within acceptable time frames.
10. Audit trail supports regulatory compliance requirements (FDCPA, CFPB, etc.).

scenarios.title: Notification Delivery Reliability and Fault Tolerance
scenarios.description: Verify that the notification system is resilient to failures and can recover gracefully without losing notifications or sending duplicates.
scenarios.testDescription: Test the reliability and fault tolerance of the collection notification system under various failure scenarios, ensuring notifications are not lost and duplicates are prevented.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Notification system with retry mechanisms is configured.
2. Test environment allows simulation of failures.
3. Message queue or notification service is available.
4. Monitoring and alerting systems are in place.
5. Test accounts are prepared for notification scenarios.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Configure notification processing for test accounts.
2. Simulate email service failure during notification delivery.
3. Verify system queues notifications for retry.
4. Restore email service and verify queued notifications are delivered.
5. Simulate database connection failure during notification generation.
6. Verify system handles failure gracefully without data loss.
7. Simulate application server crash during notification processing.
8. Verify system resumes processing after recovery without duplicates.
9. Test notification deduplication logic.
10. Verify failed notification alerts are sent to operations team.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Email service failure triggers retry mechanism automatically.
2. Notifications are queued and not lost during service outages.
3. Upon service restoration, queued notifications are delivered successfully.
4. Database failures are handled gracefully with appropriate error logging.
5. No data corruption occurs due to database failures.
6. Application crash recovery does not result in duplicate notifications.
7. Deduplication logic prevents sending same notification multiple times.
8. Maximum retry attempts are configured and respected (e.g., 3 retries).
9. Operations team receives alerts for persistent notification failures.
10. System maintains notification state across failures and restarts.
11. All recovered notifications maintain correct format with last 4 digits only.

scenarios.title: Regulatory Compliance for Collection Communications
scenarios.description: Verify that all collection lifecycle communications comply with relevant regulations such as FDCPA, TCPA, and consumer protection laws.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that the collection notification system adheres to regulatory requirements including proper disclosure language, timing restrictions, contact frequency limits, and consumer rights information.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Regulatory compliance rules are documented and implemented.
2. Notification templates include required legal language.
3. System has time-of-day and frequency restrictions configured.
4. Opt-out mechanisms are implemented.
5. Test accounts with various compliance scenarios exist.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Review all notification templates for required legal disclosures.
2. Verify FDCPA-required language is included in collection notices.
3. Test that notifications are not sent during restricted hours (e.g., before 8 AM or after 9 PM local time).
4. Verify frequency limits are enforced (e.g., not more than X calls per week).
5. Test opt-out mechanisms for various notification channels.
6. Verify that ceased communication requests are honored.
7. Check that dispute rights information is included in collection notices.
8. Verify mini-Miranda warning is included where required.
9. Test that communication to third parties is restricted as required.
10. Verify accurate identification of card issuer in all communications.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. All collection notices include required FDCPA disclosures.
2. Notifications state the amount owed, creditor name, and consumer's rights.
3. System enforces time restrictions and does not send notifications during prohibited hours.
4. Frequency limits are enforced and tracked per account.
5. Opt-out requests are processed within required timeframes (typically 24-48 hours).
6. Ceased communication requests stop all future notifications except legally permitted ones.
7. Dispute rights and validation process information is clearly stated.
8. Mini-Miranda warning appears in initial communications where required.
9. System prevents communication to unauthorized third parties.
10. All notifications accurately identify the card issuer and provide contact information.
11. Records of compliance are maintained for audit purposes.

scenarios.title: Accessibility of Collection Notifications
scenarios.description: Verify that collection lifecycle notifications are accessible to cardholders with disabilities, following WCAG guidelines for electronic communications.
scenarios.testDescription: Test that email and online notification formats comply with accessibility standards, ensuring cardholders with visual, hearing, or cognitive disabilities can access and understand collection communications.
scenarios.prerequisites:
1. Email notification templates are designed with accessibility in mind.
2. Accessibility testing tools are available.
3. WCAG 2.1 AA compliance requirements are documented.
4. Alternative format options are configured.
5. Test accounts with accessibility preferences exist.
scenarios.stepsToPerform:
1. Generate email notifications for collection lifecycle events.
2. Test email notifications with screen reader software.
3. Verify proper heading structure and semantic HTML in email templates.
4. Check color contrast ratios meet WCAG AA standards (4.5:1 for normal text).
5. Verify that important information is not conveyed by color alone.
6. Test that email content is readable when images are disabled.
7. Verify font sizes are adjustable and readable.
8. Check for alternative text on any images or icons.
9. Test keyboard navigation if interactive elements are present.
10. Verify availability of large print or Braille options for postal mail.
scenarios.expectedResult:
1. Email notifications use semantic HTML with proper heading hierarchy.
2. Screen readers can correctly interpret and read all notification content.
3. Color contrast meets or exceeds WCAG AA standards throughout.
4. Important information (amounts, dates, last 4 digits) is not dependent on color alone.
5. Email content is fully accessible with images disabled.
6. Text is readable at default sizes and can be enlarged without breaking layout.
7. All images have descriptive alternative text.
8. Keyboard navigation works for any interactive elements.
9. Large print and Braille options are available upon request.
10. Notifications are understandable at an appropriate reading level.
11. Accessibility compliance is documented and maintained.
